Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

official noun

a person in public office

also public official, government official, officials, officeholder, officer (an official)

classical

Cic. Off. 1.124
Gell. 2.2.9
M-O s.v. official: high-ranking government official

magistrātus, magistrātūs m.

noun, fourth declension

an official, a magistrate

Properly the office, then the person who holds it (Lewis & Short; see office, a public office): the officials who hold power and decide. For the staff who serve them, see civil servant.

Examples

  • Est igitur proprium mūnus magistrātūs intellegere sē gerere persōnam cīvitātis dēbēreque ejus dignitātem et decus sustinēre, servāre lēgēs, jūra discrībere, ea fideī suae commissa meminisse.

    It is the proper task of an official, then, to understand that he stands for the state, and must uphold its dignity and honour, keep the laws, give everyone their rights, and remember that these are entrusted to his good faith.Cic. Off. 1.124

  • inter fīlium magistrātum et patrem prīvātum pūblicōs honōrēs cessāre, nātūrālēs et genuīnōs exorīrī

    between a son who holds office and a father who is a private citizen, public rank gives way and the rank given by nature comes into forceGell. 2.2.9

Other words

  • appāritor, appāritōris m. — a junior official, a magistrate’s attendant

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 1.8.3; M-O s.v. official: minor government official

    The paid staff of the magistrates: lictors, clerks, messengers (Lewis & Short); see civil servant.

  • officiālis, officiālis m. — an official

    noun, third declension · also used · post-classical · Apul. Met. 1 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. official: minor government official

    A magistrate’s attendant, post-classical for appāritor (Lewis & Short); in later Latin the general word for an official. Levi and Bini (p. 29) give a description, quī mūnere fungitur, one who holds an office.

See also civil servant, office, government, mayor, officer.
